reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap front-running bot and instructs viewers to connect a wallet, confirm a transaction, and paste a bot contract address. It claims that transferring at least 0.4 BNB will produce 10x profit after a few minutes and that 90% of the profit will be returned to the user's wallet. The request to share, like, and subscribe is ordinary audience engagement rather than a financial condition for the offer.

citations.quote: HOW TO FRONT RUN PANCAKESWAP (Sniper Bot)
which automatically locates any liquidity added to a BSC token, immediately buy and sell at profit.
automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit.
until you transaction "Action" function in Remix

opening.argument: The description contains a meaningful technical limitation: this contract is designed for Binance Smart Chain and will not work on Ethereum mainnet. That is a bounded, network-specific tool description, not a representation that the mechanism works everywhere. The profit language is also conditional on profit being generated, and the supplied material does not independently establish that any return occurred or that the contract is safe. A careful judge should therefore treat the optimistic presentation as an unverified demonstration with a stated scope limitation, rather than conclusive evidence of deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet
10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool, and automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument treats the network-specific instructions and promotional wording as proof of a scam. But showing a BSC limitation is precisely the kind of qualification expected in a technical demonstration. The cited description explains an automated mechanism and its stated parameters; it does not establish that the mechanism actually produced the claimed result, that viewers were guaranteed anything, or that the creator concealed the scope.

citations.quote: This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet
which automatically locates any liquidity added to a BSC token, immediately buy and sell at profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The limitation concerns compatibility, not financial risk. The material still instructs viewers to fund the contract and presents a tenfold return after a short wait. A network qualification cannot turn a direct funding-and-profit pitch into neutral education, and the absence of independent proof does not erase the claims being made to viewers.

opening.argument: The primary presentation is an operational walkthrough for deploying and using software. It is explicitly introduced as showing viewers how to make a front-run bot, and the frames proceed through creating a contract file, pasting code, selecting Solidity, connecting a wallet, and confirming a transaction. Those are concrete instructional steps for a technology workflow. The existence of optimistic captions does not change that the observable core is a programming and deployment demonstration, for which viewers can evaluate the code and process themselves.

citations.quote: Today I will show you how to make a front run bot on bsc pancakeswap

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument calls the workflow a solicitation because it shows a wallet and discusses profit. That skips the instructional context: the material walks through Remix and contract deployment operations, while the audience-engagement request is separate from the technical steps. A tutorial can describe a tool's intended behavior without proving that every viewer will obtain the described outcome.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The steps are not merely code education: they culminate in connecting a wallet, sending at least 0.4 BNB, waiting, and expecting 10x profit. The deployment walkthrough is the delivery mechanism for the financial pitch. Calling it a tutorial does not explain why viewers are directed to transfer funds or why the promised result is presented as imminent.

opening.argument: Viewed narrowly, this is a software-tool demonstration, not evidence of a credential theft or recruitment scheme. The supplied material does not show a request for passwords, seed phrases, account credentials, or downline recruiting. It describes a contract intended for a particular blockchain and an automated trading process, while the visible workflow uses a standard development interface and wallet confirmation. Those facts support classifying the content as an operational technology presentation, with its claims requiring verification, rather than inferring additional scam mechanisms that are not shown.

citations.quote: This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument identifies a transfer instruction, but a transfer is not by itself proof that the underlying software is fraudulent. The visible process shows wallet confirmation and a contract address, not credential collection, identity impersonation, or a referral structure. The fact that the tool claims to automate trades may warrant caution, but it does not establish a hidden mechanism beyond the one described.

citations.quote: which automatically locates any liquidity added to a BSC token, immediately buy and sell at profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing credential or referral mechanism is beside the point. The demonstrated mechanism is a direct financial transfer into a contract, followed by a claimed rapid tenfold return. The frames expressly pair the minimum BNB amount with waiting and the promised profit, so the absence of passwords or downline recruiting does not make the funding pitch ordinary software commerce.
